title: request-lifecycle-compatibility-and-error-surface-for-kernel-routing
body:
Purpose

This doc collects design notes and an initial draft of the runtime API request lifecycle, the error surface we expose to callers, and the compatibility guarantees we intend to support across kernel variants, scheduler changes, and KV cache semantics. Aim is to produce an implementable compatibility matrix and a small set of consumer-facing rules we can ship with the next minor runtime release.

Context and motivation

We keep getting subtle regressions when:
- new kernels change expected request fields (e.g., chunked-kv vs fixed-kv hints),
- the scheduler begins to prefetch KV entries when batching is enabled, and
- toggles flip between per-tenant and shared cache namespaces.

Consumers expect:
- stable minimum request schema (clients should not be forced to change for patch/minor runtime upgrades),
- deterministic error semantics for transient capacity problems vs permanent configuration mismatch, and
- a clear fallback story when a preferred kernel or cache mode is unavailable.

This doc tries to tie the above together and propose explicit API-level guarantees.

High-level guarantees (proposal)

1) Backwards compatibility: Minor runtime releases MUST accept any request that conforms to the last published request schema version (currently v1). New optional fields MAY be introduced and ignored by older kernels.

2) Forward compatibility: Servers MAY return a well-defined error if a request uses a feature flag that the runtime does not support, but the error MUST be typed so clients can programmatically switch to a compatible pattern.

3) Kernel capability negotiation: Each kernel advertises a minimal capability set (capability-token in response headers during endpoint handshake). The runtime returns a capability map for the selected serving node; clients MAY request an explicit capability check as part of the request.

4) KV cache semantics: Cache locality and key-prefixing are implementation details, but we guarantee: a) cache keys are derived from request inputs in a reproducible manner documented in SDKs, b) cache hits are a performance hint — they are not a semantic contract (i.e., clients must be robust to occasional cache misses), c) when a fallback model is used due to cache invalidation, the response is the same API object shape and contains a provenance header which indicates the cache/miss/fallback reason.

Request lifecycle (sketch)

1. Client submits request-envelope (schema v1). Envelope contains: model_id, prompt (or input tokens), request_id, optional routing hint, optional kernel_hint, optional batch_key, and optional kv_cache_key_override.
2. Gateway validates basic schema & auth. If schema extension fields are unknown, gateway tags request with unknown_fields and forwards (per backward-compat rule).
3. Scheduler evaluates routing policy: region, cost-tier, latency-SLO, kernel capabilities. Scheduler selects node(s) and preferred kernel.
4. Selected node performs capability check. If capability mismatch (client asked for kernel_hint not available), runtime returns a typed error (see Error Codes) and a suggested fallback token.
5. If KV cache is enabled for model, compute cache key (deterministic) and attempt cache lookup. Cache lookup may be synchronous (fast path) or asynchronous (prefetch path) depending on batch and scheduler mode.
6. If cache hit and cache-provenance policy allows, return cached response with headers (x-rw-cache-status: HIT/STALE/EXPIRED) and x-rw-provenance.
7. On cache miss, dispatch to kernel. Kernel executes; interim partial streaming frames may be produced. Kernel uses same request envelope for deterministic logging and correctness.
8. On completion runtime may insert into cache based on cache policy; insertion is best-effort and does not change the returned response.

Schema notes and fields (draft)

- request_id: required, client-generated UUID.
- model_id: required, includes pinned model version.
- kernel_hint: optional enum [fast-token, high-quality, quantized-x8, attn-optimized]. If set, server may return KERNEL_UNAVAILABLE.
- batch_key: optional string. Used by scheduler to group batching; must be stable for identical prompts to get KV cache benefits.
- kv_cache_key_override: optional string. Advanced, rarely used. Overrides derived cache key. Using this makes the request non-idempotent across runtime config changes; returns WARNING in x-rw-provenance when used.
- feature_flags: optional list of short strings for experimental toggles; unknown flags MUST NOT break normal execution — server returns UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE if a flag is required for safety.

Error codes (initial taxonomy)

Format: error.code is a short upper_snake string, error.message is human readable, error.metadata contains structured hints (in headers). We will expose the following top-level codes:

- INVALID_SCHEMA: request failed validation (client must change payload).
- AUTH_FAILURE: creds invalid or insufficient.
- QUOTA_EXCEEDED: usage-related throttling.
- KERNEL_UNAVAILABLE: requested kernel_hint cannot be satisfied on chosen node. Client should retry without kernel_hint or with suggested alternative_kernel in headers.
- SCHEDULER_REJECTED: transient overload; includes retry_after header.
- CACHE_MISCONFIG: KV cache requested but not configured for model/tenant. Return includes configuration key and migration doc link.
- INTERNAL_RUNTIME_ERROR: catch-all for server-side problems; includes incident id.

Error handling semantics

- Deterministic vs transient: We mark errors as either deterministic (client change required) or transient (retry with backoff). KERNEL_UNAVAILABLE can be either — if client requested a kernel_hint that no node in the cluster ever supports, it is deterministic; if it's due to temporary unavailability it is transient. The runtime must include a deterministic boolean in metadata.

- Suggested fallbacks: Errors that can be mitigated by client action MUST include a suggested action hint in headers (e.g., Retry-Without-KernelHint, Use-Alternate-Model, Wait-30s).

KV cache behavior and guarantees

- Key derivation: by default: sha256(model_version + batch_key + stable_prompt_normalization). Normalization steps are listed in SDK docs.
- Cache consistency: we do NOT guarantee strong consistency. For model version rollouts, we guarantee eventual coherence: after model version pin change, cache entries for the old model will be invalidated within N seconds (configurable per deployment).
- Cache namespace isolation: tenant-level isolation is the default. Shared caches are opt-in and must be explicitly enabled in model config.
- Cache headers: x-rw-cache-status: MISS/HIT/STALE/EXPIRED, x-rw-cache-age: seconds, x-rw-provenance: source (kernel/model/cached) and a short reason text.

Kernel routing and scheduler hints

- The scheduler uses two inputs: kernel capability sets and request hints (batch_key, kernel_hint, latency_slo).
- We propose an orthogonal capability vector (latencyClass, quantizationSupport, attentionMode) rather than stringly-typed kernel names. This lets us map new kernels into capability buckets without breaking clients.
- Clients MAY express a soft_preference for capabilities and provide fallbacks. The runtime will prefer nodes that match the full vector but will fall back to the closest match if allowed by request flags.

Streaming and partial responses

- If a request triggers streaming, we guarantee the same streaming envelope shape across minor versions. Streaming control frames: start, chunk, end, error. Error frames must provide the same error taxonomy as full responses.

Observability and headers (consumer facing)

We will surface a minimal set of headers so clients can decide runtime behavior:
- x-rw-node-id
- x-rw-selected-kernel
- x-rw-cache-status
- x-rw-capabilities (short token)
- x-rw-error-type
- x-rw-incident (when INTERNAL_RUNTIME_ERROR)

Open questions (action items)

1) Do we need a formal capability registry (confluence page exists) and a stable capability token format? (Owner: Diego)
2) Should kv_cache_key_override be allowed for hosted API at all? Risks: makes caching non-deterministic across provider upgrades. (Owner: Maya)
3) What is the invalidation window for model rollouts? Suggested default: 300s. Ops must confirm with Dedicated team. (Owner: Liam)
4) How do we expose per-request per-token billing when cache hits avoid model execution? Billing & audit needs clear provenance — product to weigh in. (Linked JIRA: JIRA-BILL-77)

Next steps

- Socialize this doc in eng-serving-runtime weekly sync (next meeting: 2025-03-05).
- Draft an API spec PR for gateway-level headers and error shapes (PR owner: Ava).
- Prototype capability-token handshake in the node bootstrap flow (Spike ticket: ENG-1488).

Notes to reviewers

This is intentionally pragmatic: it accepts that caches are best-effort and that kernels will evolve. The core goal is to provide a small, stable set of client-visible guarantees that reduce brittle client logic and make rollouts safer. Please comment inline, add concrete compatibility needs you know of, or tag myself/Diego if you'd like to work on artifacts.
